catalog_quote: Languages of Sumba have vowel epenthesis (a.k.a. paragoge). Certain words with a final consonant undergo epenthesis in order to create a final open syllable. The epenthetic vowel is extra-metrical and does not shift stress from the penultimate vowel of the root. In Kambera the epenthetic vowel is [u]. Examples include: *quzan > uraŋ → uraŋ-u ‘rain’, *tasik > tehik → tehik-u ‘sea’, and *umpu > umbuk → umbuk-u ‘grandchild’ (Klamer 1998a: 19). In Weyewa, Loli, and Mamboru the epenthetic vowel is usually [a] (though exceptions occur); as in Weyewa tazik-a ‘sea’ and Mamboru umbuk-a ‘grandchild’. In Kodi the epenthetic vowel is [o].

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the penultimate vowel of the root; the paragogic final vowel (Mamboru -a, e.g. umbuk-a) is extrametrical and does not count, so such words surface with antepenultimate stress. This is a family-level generalisation over the languages of Sumba in a comparative handbook, applied to Mamboru by name; it is not drawn from a first-hand description of Mamboru (none exists). Consistent supporting evidence: Wielenga 1910 (Sumbanese from Kambera, with Memboro dialect notes) 'als een regel valt de klemtoon op de voorlaatste lettergreep.. De facultatieve sluit oe telt niet als lettergreep', and Wielenga 1917's dialect survey flags only Lamboja and Kodi as deviating in klemtoon, not Memboro.
new_statements.exceptions: Only that the quality of the Mamboru epenthetic vowel has exceptions ('usually [a] (though exceptions occur)'); no stress exceptions given for Mamboru.
new_statements.domain_note: Root/word level; paragogic vowel excluded from the count. Mamboru forms in this source are taken from Onvlee 1984 (dictionary data collected 1920-1950).
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to the same variety: Mamboru/Memboro/Mamboro [mvd], mamb1305, kecamatan Mamboru, north coast of central Sumba (ABVD list from desa Wendewa Selatan, with Cendana variants). Grimes & Edwards 2026 class it as the non-denasalising member of 'Central Sumba' (*s = s); Glottolog 5.1 places it in a 'Kambera' node with Kambera (kamb1299). The Wielenga 1910 klemtoon rule is explicitly for the Kambera dialect (kamb1299), not Mamboru.

new_statements.quote: Deze sluiters worden klinkend gemaakt door middel van een steunvocaal, die ze voor wegvallen bewaart, nl. u in het gehele oostelijke taalgebied, behalve Mamboru, a in het gehele westelijke taalgebied en in Mamboru en o in het kodisch. Invloed op het accent, dat als regel valt op de eerste lettergreep van het stamwoord, heeft deze vocaal niet, behalve in Kodi. [...] Het kodisch laat onder invloed van de steunvocaal het accent verspringen, indien de vocaal in de eerste lettergreep kort is, bijv. Mamboru bàndjala, Anakalang bidjalu, Wewewa bòndala, Kodi bandálo, wegbergen; [Mamboru] làpita [...] Kodi lepéto, vouwen; [Mamboru] sàlata [...] Kodi haláto, bezien (p.166). [...] de à en de gerekte klinkers (e, i, o, u) komen alleen voor in de geaccentueerde lettergreep van het stamwoord (p.167).
new_statements.translation: These final consonants are made pronounceable by means of a support vowel, which keeps them from being dropped, namely u in the whole eastern language area except Mamboru, a in the whole western language area and in Mamboru, and o in Kodi. This vowel has no influence on the accent, which as a rule falls on the first syllable of the stem word, except in Kodi. [...] Kodi, under the influence of the support vowel, lets the accent shift if the vowel of the first syllable is short, e.g. Mamboru bàndjala, Anakalang bidjalu, Wewewa bòndala, Kodi bandálo 'put away'; Mamboru làpita ... Kodi lepéto 'fold'; Mamboru sàlata ... Kodi haláto 'look at'. [...] the à and the lengthened vowels (e, i, o, u) occur only in the accented syllable of the stem word.

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the catalog record (Grimes & Edwards 2026: stress on the penultimate vowel of the root, epenthetic/paragogic vowel extrametrical, Mamboru paragogic vowel usually [a]) and adds first-hand, Mamboru-specific detail 90 years older: accent-marked Mamboru forms (bàndjala, làpita, sàlata; taşika/lapita/kikira/ikita in the p.167 table), the formulation of the domain as the stem ('eerste lettergreep van het stamwoord'), the explicit statement that the support vowel a of Mamboru does not move the accent (unlike Kodi o), and the restriction of long vowels/à to the accented stem syllable. Note for the catalog's surface template penultimate stress: both Onvlee and Grimes & Edwards place…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Onvlee (writing in 1936 from his own fieldwork, and naming Mamboru explicitly) states that in Sumbanese, Mamboru included, the accent as a rule falls on the first syllable of the stem word (stamwoord); Sumbanese stems are canonically disyllabic, so this is the penultimate syllable of the root. Consonant-final stems take a paragogic support vowel (a in Mamboru, as in the west; u elsewhere in the east; o in Kodi) which does NOT affect the accent in Mamboru (only Kodi shifts the accent rightward onto the stem's second syllable), so surface forms with the paragogic vowel are stressed on the antepenult: Mamboru bàndjala 'put away', làpita 'fold', sàlata 'look at' (grave accent = Onvlee's stress mark) against Kodi bandálo, lepéto, haláto. Long vowels and à occur only in the accented stem syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: 'als regel' (as a rule) hedges the stem-initial placement without listing exceptions for Mamboru; the only named deviation is Kodi, where the support vowel pulls the accent onto the second stem syllable when the first stem vowel is short (bandálo, lepéto, hawóloto, haláto), also under suffixation of grammatical elements. Lamboja is noted (p.167) for deleting unaccented stem vowels (làpta < làpita), not for a different accent placement. Monosyllabic stems with a long vowel are said to arise from contraction.
new_statements.identity_note: Onvlee treats 'het sumbaas' as one language with eastern and western dialect groups and names Mamboru (landschap Mamboru, north-west Sumba, on the east/west border with Tana Righu) as an eastern dialect that shares the western support vowel a; the accent statement is made for Sumbanese generally with Mamboru forms cited explicitly in the comparative tables (pp.166-168). His base of description is Wewewa, 'met verwijzing naar andere dialecten'.
